description: CORE tool parity part B: browser-lifecycle + observation tools that require evolving BrowserSession. Add multi-tab support (browser_tabs list/create/close/select), browser_handle_dialog (accept/dismiss dialogs), browser_file_upload (into a file chooser), browser_take_screenshot (PNG/JPEG/WebP), browser_console_messages, browser_network_requests (list), browser_network_request (one request in detail), browser_run_code_unsafe (guarded Playwright snippet execution). This feature evolves src/browser.ts to own MULTIPLE pages/tabs and to register dialog/console/network listeners, confining all Playwright API growth to that boundary.
steps: Evolve src/browser.ts BrowserSession to manage multiple tabs: keep a pages array + an activePage index; getPage() returns the active page; add listTabs(): TabInfo[], newTab(url?), closeTab(index), selectTab(index). Preserve the lazy-launch + concurrency-serialisation behaviour and the resolveRef contract (resolveRef operates on the active page). On context creation, attach listeners that accumulate console messages (ConsoleMessageRecord[]) and network requests (NetworkRequestRecord[], captured via page.on('request')/('response') or context.on) into ring-buffered arrays exposed via getters. Add a dialog-handler registration: a method to set the next-dialog disposition (accept/dismiss + optional promptText) that a page.on('dialog') handler consults. Add a helper to run a raw Playwright code snippet against the page (used by run_code_unsafe) confined here.

browser_tabs: new src/tools/tabs.ts. args { action: 'list'|'create'|'close'|'select', index?: number, url?: string }. Delegate to the new BrowserSession tab methods. Return a textResult listing tabs (index/title/url/active) for list, snapshotResult for create/select. CORE.

browser_handle_dialog: new src/tools/handle_dialog.ts. args { accept: boolean, promptText?: string }. Register the disposition on the session so the NEXT dialog is handled; return textResult confirming. Because dialogs are triggered by a subsequent action, the fixture test will set disposition then trigger a confirm() and assert the outcome. CORE.

browser_file_upload: new src/tools/file_upload.ts. args { paths: string[] }. Use page.waitForEvent('filechooser') coordination OR set files on a file input target; follow Playwright MCP semantics (respond to a pending file chooser). Provide args { element?, target?, paths }. If target is a file input, locator.setInputFiles(paths). CORE.

browser_take_screenshot: new src/tools/take_screenshot.ts. args { type?: 'png'|'jpeg'|'webp', fullPage?: boolean, element?, target?, filename?: string }. Capture via page.screenshot / locator.screenshot with the chosen type. Return an MCP image content block ({ type: 'image', data: base64, mimeType }) — extend shared.ts ToolResult content typing to allow an image block. Assert non-empty base64 in the test. CORE.
browser_console_messages: new src/tools/console_messages.ts. No args (optionally { onlyErrors?: boolean }). Return the accumulated ConsoleMessageRecord[] from the session as textResult. CORE.
browser_network_requests: new src/tools/network_requests.ts. No args. Return the accumulated NetworkRequestRecord[] (method/url/status) as textResult. CORE.
browser_network_request: new src/tools/network_request.ts. args { url: string } or { index: number } to select one recorded request; return its full detail (headers, status, resourceType). CORE.

browser_run_code_unsafe: new src/tools/run_code_unsafe.ts. args { code: string }. GUARD given the name: gate it behind an explicit config flag (e.g. config.allowUnsafeCode from LAYA_ALLOW_UNSAFE_CODE, default false) AND keep it CORE only in the sense of always-listed but refusing with a clear message when the flag is off. Execute the snippet via the browser boundary helper (new Function/page context) and return the result. Document the risk in the description. When the flag is off, return an isError textResult explaining it is disabled.
Register all in the registry (run_code_unsafe honoring its flag). Update ASSIST_TOOL_NAMES.

Tests in test/core-tools.test.ts (or a new test/core-lifecycle.test.ts): tabs creates a second tab and list shows 2 tabs; handle_dialog accept lets a confirm() proceed (assert the fixture's post-dialog DOM state) and dismiss cancels it; screenshot returns non-empty base64 image content of a fixture; console_messages captures a console.log a fixture fired on load; network_requests lists a request the fixture made (e.g. it fetches a same-origin resource); network_request returns detail for that request; file_upload sets a file on an input and the input reflects it; run_code_unsafe returns a value when enabled and refuses when disabled. Add fixtures (dialog.html, console.html, network.html, upload.html) that produce these literal outcomes offline.
acceptance_criteria: BrowserSession manages multiple tabs and exposes console/network buffers + dialog disposition, all Playwright usage confined to src/browser.ts.
browser_tabs creates and lists a second tab.
browser_take_screenshot returns a non-empty base64 image content block.
browser_console_messages captures a console.log fired by a fixture.
browser_network_requests lists a request the fixture made; browser_network_request returns its detail.
browser_handle_dialog accept/dismiss produce the correct literal DOM outcomes.
browser_run_code_unsafe is gated by a config flag and refuses when disabled.
typecheck + build + full test suite green offline.
findings: Implemented all 8 tools plus BrowserSession multi-tab/console/network/dialog/runCode evolution. Notes for later features: (1) BrowserSession now owns a pages[] + activeIndex; getPage() returns the active page, resolveRef() acts on the active page. Kept the await getPage() before resolveRef() contract in every new ref-based tool. (2) trackPage() attaches console/pageerror/request/response/requestfailed/dialog listeners to EVERY page (including new tabs) so buffers are session-wide; buffers are ring-capped at 500. (3) Dialog handling is one-shot: setNextDialog() registers a disposition consumed by the next page.on('dialog'); handle_dialog registers it, the caller then triggers the action. (4) Added config.allowUnsafeCode (LAYA_ALLOW_UNSAFE_CODE, default false via envBoolDefaultFalse) threaded config->server->ToolContext.allowUnsafeCode; run_code_unsafe is always registered (CORE) but refuses with isError when the flag is off. (5) shared.ts ToolResult content is now ContentBlock = TextContent | ImageContent; added imageResult(); textResult unchanged. (6) Playwright 1.63 screenshot supports png|jpeg|webp. (7) Network test fetches a SAME-ORIGIN loopback resource (network-data.html) served by the fixture server, staying fully offline. New fixtures: dialog.html, console.html, network.html, network-data.html, upload.html. Tests in test/core-lifecycle.test.ts each use an isolated BrowserSession so console/network buffers do not bleed across cases. Verification: typecheck + build clean, full suite 87 passed / 2 skipped offline (baseline was 77/2).
